title: The Samanid mausoleum is built at Bukhara
summary: The tomb associated with Ismail Samani at Bukhara belongs to the tenth century. Its preserved architecture stands within a city whose institutions and urban fabric developed over many later periods.

claims.text: The tomb associated with Ismail Samani at Bukhara belongs to the tenth century. Its preserved architecture stands within a city whose institutions and urban fabric developed over many later periods.

A single surviving monument can anchor a comparison without supplying dates for an entire culture. The mausoleum should remain distinct from the city’s seventeenth-century religious schools and earlier settlement.
